content:
Apple's first foldable iPhone is expected to make its official debut just over a week from now. Reports indicate that during the development process, Apple internally considered launching a brand-new Apple Pencil designed to work with the iPhone Ultra, though this stylus is very likely to never actually hit the market.

The information comes from Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, who wanted to emphasise that this Apple Pencil should not be announced next month. Nonetheless, he has detailed what the stylus was originally supposed to look like and how it was meant to work.

It was originally not going to be the same as the Apple Pencil used by the current iPad lineup; it was designed to be 'shorter' to match the shorter height of the iPhone Ultra's body. However, similar to the iPad version of the Apple Pencil, it was originally going to attach magnetically to the side of the device for convenient storage and charging.

He pointed out that holding the stylus while using the iPhone Ultra would be rather awkward, because the stylus would stick to the side of the device; by comparison, with an iPad, when you use the device in landscape orientation, the stylus attaches to the top.

He also mentioned that this stylus would very likely leave 'unsightly marks' on the more delicate inner display of the iPhone Ultra.

He ultimately speculated that the main reason Apple decided not to release this stylus was to avoid contradicting the stance Steve Jobs took when he unveiled the original iPhone — 'Who wants a stylus?'

I personally still think that an Apple Pencil for the iPhone Ultra would be quite practical, but it looks like we won't be seeing this stylus for the time being.

After the most recent round of price hikes, it might be worth checking out Apple's refurbished product store for deals — various types of refurbished products can save you quite a bit, including iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Apple TV.
